paper.title: F.784 Treasury Management Activity Report 2025/26
paper.note: Covering report is a 4-page brief. Substance lives in two companion papers already on disk and read in full: doc 39486 (Annex A, 14 pp, Annual Treasury Management Review) and doc 39487 (Annex B, 5 pp, Pooled Fund Investments). All figures below sourced from Annex A/B unless the covering report itself is cited. The same F.784 report is repeated at Audit Committee on 2 July 2026 (doc 39527/39528/39529) and at Full Council on 23 July 2026 (doc 39621/39622/39623 under a re-numbered F.791) — content identical, no re-read needed.

facts.value: £0 external borrowing at 31.3.26. No temporary loans, no PWLB, no market debt, no LOBOs, no other long-term liabilities. Position unchanged from 31.3.25; no borrowing taken out during 2025/26.
facts.note: Six independent presentations across Annex A all agree at zero (Table 1, Table 2, §5, Table 7, §9.7 debt row, §9.8). The PWLB price book returns no borrower matching 'Forest of Dean' — both sides tie at zero. This is not a live PWLB position; there is no loan book to reconcile.

facts.value: General Fund CFR £0 at 31.3.26 actual; forecast to rise to £4.220m (31.3.27), £6.090m (31.3.28) and £5.941m (31.3.29). Liability benchmark table forecasts external borrowing of £5.878m from 31.3.27, tapering to £5.508m by 31.3.29. Net loans requirement moves from £(14.191)m (net investor) at 31.3.26 to +£1.125m (net borrower) at 31.3.29.
facts.note: The Council is scheduled to become a first-time PWLB borrower over the strategy period. However Annex B §1.7 explicitly states the plan is to fund emerging capital pressure by selling pooled fund investments rather than borrowing: 'the potential sale of pooled fund investments will be evaluated in line with capital programme needs and timing considerations. To minimise financial impact, any divestment should ideally begin with the fund that presents the smallest capital loss, offers the lowest return, and is the most readily accessible.' Small figures either way.

facts.value: Total investments £14.349m at 31.3.26 (down from £16.064m at 31.3.25). Split: long-term £6.566m at 4.56%, short-term £2.139m at 4.14%, cash £5.644m at 4.14%. Whole-portfolio rate 4.57%. Detail: banks & building societies £0.306m at 3.51%; local authority £2.003m at 6.75%; money market funds £5.338m at 4.14%; CCLA Property £2.673m at 4.11%; CCLA Cautious Multi Asset £1.775m at 2.83%; Schroders Equity Income £0.944m at 6.25%; Fundamentum REIT £1.310m at 3.00%.
facts.note: Local Authority line at 6.75% is significantly higher than any other treasury asset in the book. Portfolio ranged between £12.865m and £27.480m during the year. Average investment portfolio £20.05m at outturn (Annex A §7).

facts.value: £6m original investment across three strategic pooled funds (CCLA Property £3m, CCLA Cautious Multi Asset £2m, Schroders Income Maximiser £1m) plus £2m in Fundamentum Social Housing REIT. Cumulative unrealised capital loss to date £1,434,283 (funds £714,283, REIT £720,000). Dividend income to date £2,285,293 across all four. 2025/26 dividend income £302,462 at 4.56% blended return on £8m original.
facts.note: IFRS 9 statutory override extended to 1 April 2029 for investments in place before 1 April 2024 (all four funds were entered between 2017 and 2019). Fundamentum REIT NAV drop 'mainly due to a reduction of around 20% in property valuations ... financial difficulties experienced by some housing associations in the specialist supported housing sector' — Annex B §1.8. CCLA Property fund has 6 months' notice; other two funds 2 business days'; REIT variable (direct, via Arlingclose network, or property sale).

facts.value: Investment income budget £849,000 (original), £789,000 (revised), actual £797,626 — surplus £8,626 vs revised, deficit £51,374 vs original. Overall return 4.57% (24/25 comparator 4.46%). Debt interest paid £2k on £25k budget.
facts.note: Covering §2.2 and Annex A §3.1 both foot to the £8,626 surplus. No borrowing was taken during the year so the £2k of debt interest paid appears to relate to a de minimis fee — the paper does not itemise it.

facts.value: Portfolio average credit A+ at 31.3.26 (target A-). Liquidity £11.860m within 3 months (target £5m). Long-term principal invested £8m (limit £10m). Interest rate exposure ±£138,078 on 1% shift (limit ±£220,000). All 10 investment sub-limits complied. Debt: authorised limit £10m (per §9.8) or £20m (per §8 Table 7), operational boundary £5m or £10m — the two tables disagree; actual £0 all year, so no compliance question.
facts.note: Six-month ranging period for treasury cash £12.865m-£27.480m. The debt-limits inconsistency between §8 Table 7 (Op'l Boundary £10m, Auth Limit £20m) and §9.8 (£5m, £10m) is an internal-only observation — not raised. Signal 'none' — verified quiet on borrowing.

facts.value: Adviser: Arlingclose Ltd. Bank Rate fell 0.75% from 4.50% (1 April 2025) to 3.75% (31 March 2026). Arlingclose's post-March MPC forecast at Annex A §2.7: 'Bank Rate will be held at 3.75%' with near-term upside risks from the US/Israel-Iran conflict outlook.
facts.note: DMADF deposits ranged 4.13-4.56% during 25/26; money market rates 3.81-4.50%. Bank Rate today (2026-08-15) is 3.75% — the hold has continued to date.

Both sides tie at zero: our book holds no PWLB loans for this council, and Annex A §5 says the Council 'held no temporary loans. The year-end borrowing position and the year-on-year change remained the same as at 31st March 2025 with no borrowing taken out during the year.'
reconciliation.balance_sheet_identity: Applied at 31.3.26 using §9.6 CFR figure. CFR £0 − external borrowing £0 − other long-term liabilities £0 = internal borrowing £0. The Council is a net investor by £14.349m (Annex A Table 2). Note that the Loans CFR figure in §8.3 (£0.430m at 31.3.26 actual) does not agree with §9.6's £0 CFR or Table 1's £0 CFR — an internal inconsistency in the paper. See INTERNAL notes in the extract. Using the higher £0.430m figure the identity still holds trivially — £0.430m − £0 − £0 = £0.430m of internal borrowing against £14.349m investments.
reconciliation.budget_tie: Investment income £797,626 actual vs £789,000 revised = surplus £8,626 (covering §2.2 = Annex A §3.1 = Annex A §7). All three cite the same £8,626 figure. Return 4.57% on £20.05m average portfolio (Annex A §7). 4.57% also appears as the whole-portfolio rate in Table 3 and as the outturn rate in Table 5 — two different bases but the paper uses the same number.
reconciliation.pooled_fund_tie: Annex B Table 1 capital loss to date sums to £1,434,283 exactly: (359,760) + (235,620) + (118,903) + (720,000). Annex A Table 4 splits the same total as 'Total Current Pooled Funds £(714,283)' plus 'Total Equity Investment £(720,000)' = £(1,434,283). Ties across annexes. Table 1a annual dividend total £(302,462) ties to Table 4's £242,462 pooled funds + £60,000 REIT (Annex A prints the REIT dividend as £60,750 vs Annex B's £60,000 — £750 difference, un-reconciled).
reconciliation.rates_check: Not applicable — no PWLB debt on either side, no rates to compare. The prevailing PWLB 10-year certainty rate on 14 August 2026 (5.83%, notice 314/26 PM) is quoted in other notes but is not a meaningful cross-check for a council with zero external borrowing and no drawdown planned inside a year.

summary.text:
Forest of Dean District Council's 2025/26 Treasury Management Outturn is a debt-free council's outturn: no PWLB, no LOBOs, no market debt, no temporary borrowing, no PFI or lease liabilities. The Council entered 2025/26 with zero external debt, held zero all year, and closed the year the same way (Annex A §5, Table 2, Table 7, §9.7 all agree). Our PWLB price book returns no borrower matching Forest of Dean; both sides of the reconciliation tie at zero and there is no loan book to compare.

The Council is a net investor with £14.349m of treasury investments at 31 March 2026 (down from £16.064m at 31 March 2025 — Annex A Table 2). The portfolio splits £8.705m of core treasury (banks, MMFs, LA deposit, cash) yielding 4.14-6.75%, plus £5.758m in four strategic pooled funds (three CCLA/Schroders funds plus Fundamentum Social Housing REIT). The pooled-fund carrying value understates the £8m original investment by £1,434,283 of unrealised capital loss to date (£714,283 on the three funds; £720,000 on the REIT alone, following a 20% write-down in property valuations across the specialist supported housing sector — Annex B §1.8). The IFRS 9 statutory override for these unrealised losses is expected to extend to 1 April 2029 for investments in place before 1 April 2024 (Annex A §6, Annex B §1.4), which shelters revenue from the mark-to-market position until that date.

The paper forecasts a shift into external borrowing over the strategy period — General Fund CFR climbs from £0 (31.3.26 actual) to £4.220m (31.3.27), £6.090m (31.3.28) and £5.941m (31.3.29) per §9.6, with the liability benchmark table at §8.3 scheduling external borrowing of £5.878m from 31.3.27 onwards. But Annex B §1.7 is explicit that the Council's plan is to fund emerging capital pressure by selling pooled fund investments rather than borrowing: 'To minimise financial impact, any divestment should ideally begin with the fund that presents the smallest capital loss, offers the lowest return, and is the most readily accessible.' Whether the borrowing forecast in §8.3 actually materialises depends on the divestment decision.

Investment income £797,626 ran £8,626 above the revised budget of £789,000 (£51,374 below the original £849,000), at a whole-portfolio rate of 4.57% against 4.46% the prior year — Annex A §7. All prudential indicators complied. Portfolio credit rating A+ against A- target. Adviser: Arlingclose Ltd.

The paper carries a number of internal inconsistencies (CFR figure disagrees across three tables; debt-limits table appears twice with different figures; header on §9.3 mis-labels capital expenditure as CFR; empty commercial-investment table; verbatim-duplicated paragraphs; template not updated from prior year). These are noted INTERNAL ONLY in the extract — not raised, because the S151 has signed the paper and pointing them out risks looking like a correction. The substance underneath is coherent: this is a debt-free district council with £14m of investments and a small forecast capital financing need it plans to meet from divestment.

From a PWLB pricing platform perspective this paper is thin — there is no live loan book to reconcile, no refinancing risk, no LOBO, no break-cost position, no discount to price. The forward-borrowing signal is small (£5-6m) and the paper's own plan is to avoid borrowing by selling pooled funds. There is no PWLB angle we could offer that goes beyond what the paper itself already carries. Per PIPELINE.md this is a correct case for a thin note with no email drafted.

status.note: Read in full: covering report (doc 39485, 4pp), Annex A Annual Treasury Management Review (doc 39486, 14pp), Annex B Pooled Fund Investments (doc 39487, 5pp). All three PDFs held locally; no fetching from the council site. The paper is thin from a PWLB perspective because the Council is debt-free: no external borrowing at any point in 2025/26, no PWLB loans on our price book (both sides tie at zero — nothing to reconcile). Forward CFR ramp of £4-6m from 27/28 is small and Annex B §1.7 explicitly states the Council's plan is to divest pooled funds rather than borrow to meet emerging capital pressure. Balance-sheet identity trivially holds: CFR £0 − external £0 − OLTL £0 = £0 internal borrowing, against £14.349m of net investments. Per PIPELINE.md 'a thin note is far better than a padded one' — draft NO email, this is a correct outcome. Officer address IS published (Andrew Knott, andrew.knott@publicagroup.uk) so this council is not blocked on address; it is blocked on hook. Should the Council actually enter the PWLB market when forecast, or should a mid-year report show discretionary divestment triggered, revisit.
